solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Perhaps Juno will have firm date by start of Easter term

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, so only the opening letter of Easter is used

parts.note: a term is a word

explanation.surface: A student hopes for a firm date for something to happen before the Easter term begins.
explanation.walkthrough: Juno was the name given to one of the D-Day landing beaches in 1944, an operational label rather than a goddess here; 'Perhaps' flags it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Juno was a wartime operational name, so it is an example of a secret label of that kind.

clue.text: Type of gas with variable heat unit

parts.note: Calor is a brand of bottled gas sold in Britain
Y is a common algebra symbol for a variable

explanation.surface: A kind of gas with a fluctuating heat output.
explanation.walkthrough: Calor gas is a familiar British brand of bottled propane and butane.
explanation.definitionFit: A variant spelling of the standard measure of heat energy used in physics and dieting.

clue.text: Injecting iodine into clot aids dispersing of cardiac dilation

indicators.note: injecting means putting one thing into another, so a letter goes inside the jumbled word
dispersing means scattering, so the letters of clot aids are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: I is the chemical symbol for iodine

explanation.surface: A medical treatment: inject iodine into a clot to help dissolve it, in a heart condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dispersing' scrambles CLOT AIDS, and 'Injecting' puts I among those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes the phase when the heart's chambers relax and expand to fill with blood.

clue.text: Wide extremity of faith is important for spirit in Dublin

parts.note: W is the cricket abbreviation for a wide

indicators.note: the extremity of a word is its tip, here the last letter of faith

parts.note: key means important or crucial

explanation.surface: Broad-minded faith matters greatly for the Irish spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in Dublin' points to the Irish spelling with an E.
explanation.definitionFit: A distilled liquor, spelt with an E in Ireland and the US but without it for Scotch.

clue.text: Storms take a lot of time

parts.note: R stands for recipe, Latin for take, on prescriptions
ages means a long time

explanation.surface: Bad weather systems can last for a very long time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Storms' is a verb, meaning shows fury.
explanation.definitionFit: To storm is to shout angrily or behave violently, which is a synonym for raving furiously.

clue.text: Mature winner?

definitions.meaning: ... Mature was a Hollywood film actor, so his first name fills the gap
one who triumphs in a contest

explanation.surface: Is the winner of the contest the older, more seasoned competitor?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mature' looks like an adjective but is the surname of the actor Victor Mature.
explanation.definitionFit: The actor's forename is the first sense; the second is a plain synonym for someone who triumphs.

clue.text: Visible awareness

definitions.meaning: split as two words, it means able to be seen

explanation.surface: An understanding that can be plainly seen.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it means within view; as one it means perception or understanding.

clue.text: Note bits of ice glistening near river in Devon

parts.note: te is a note of the tonic sol-fa scale

indicators.note: bits of means small pieces, here the opening letters of ice and glistening

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for near

explanation.surface: Remark on flecks of ice shining by a Devon river.
explanation.walkthrough: Devon is a county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Teign flows through Devon to the sea at Teignmouth, so it is an example of a local watercourse.

clue.text: Hired protesters scattered near tomb

indicators.note: scattered means spread about, so the letters of near tomb are rearranged

explanation.surface: Paid demonstrators dispersed close to a grave.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a crowd paid or recruited to demonstrate, used scornfully of agitators.

clue.text: Old European revolutionary boy's vulgar endlessly

indicators.note: revolutionary means overturning, so the remaining letters are rearranged
endlessly means with the ends removed, so the first and last letters of the phrase go

explanation.surface: An old European rebel's son speaks crudely without stopping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' drops B and R from BOYSVULGAR, leaving OYSVULGA for 'revolutionary' to rearrange. 'revolutionary' tempts as a reversal of 'boy' as GUY, which fails.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of Yugoslavia, a former Balkan state that broke up in the 1990s, so a historic nationality.

clue.text: Principal seeking independence — relating to this may give the desired answer

definitions.text: this may give the desired answer

parts.note: principal means chief or leading
a quest is a seeking or search
I is the abbreviation for independence or independent
on means about or relating to

explanation.surface: A head teacher who seeks independence from the authority is questioned in a way that prompts the reply wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: A courtroom term for a query phrased to suggest its own reply, which a lawyer uses to get the response wanted.

clue.text: Further shots of skater whirling full of energy

indicators.note: full of means the spun word holds the next piece inside it
whirling suggests spinning around, so the letters of skater are mixed up

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A film crew needs more footage of an energetic skater spinning on the ice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'whirling' turns SKATER into RETAKS, and 'full of' puts E inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: In filming, scenes shot again are repeats of earlier takes, so additional shots are this.

clue.text: South Africa newspaper's leader is flimsy stuff

parts.note: an organ is a newspaper or periodical serving as a mouthpiece; as the leader it comes in front of the next piece
ZA is the international code for South Africa

explanation.surface: A South African paper's editorial is dismissed as insubstantial stuff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' looks like an editorial but says the newspaper word leads, going before ZA.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin, stiff, sheer silk or synthetic fabric, so light material is a fair description.

clue.text: Quietly set down delivery and co-operate

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quietly
to lay is to set down
in cricket a delivery is a ball bowled

explanation.surface: A bowler quietly puts down a delivery and agrees to go along with things.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom meaning to go along with others' wishes, to work together rather than obstruct.

clue.text: Supply comments during the year on gallery

parts.note: anno is Latin for in the year
the Tate is a famous London art gallery

explanation.surface: Provide remarks throughout the year about an art gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tate is a group of art galleries in Britain, chiefly in London.
explanation.definitionFit: To add explanatory notes or remarks to a text, which is to provide commentary on it.

clue.text: Intrinsically promotes convenience store

indicators.note: intrinsically means in its inner nature, so the letters are found inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A shop that pushes the idea of convenience at its very core.
explanation.walkthrough: 'convenience store' reads as one phrase, but only 'store' defines; 'convenience' is part of the hiding place.
explanation.definitionFit: Tesco is a major British supermarket chain, so it is an example of a retailer.

clue.text: Husky's ear?!

parts.note: a husk is a shell, so husky can mean like a shell; the phrase is also British slang for an ear

explanation.surface: Pointing at a sled dog's ear.
explanation.walkthrough: Husky looks like the dog, but read as 'husk-like' it describes the shape; 'shell-like' is jokey British slang for an ear, as in 'a word in your shell-like'.
explanation.definitionFit: Husky read as 'resembling a husk' means shaped like a shell, and that adjective is slang for an ear.

clue.text: Prisoner joined in disorder

parts.note: con is short for convict, a prisoner
fused means joined together

explanation.surface: An inmate was linked up in a chaotic state.
explanation.definitionFit: Jumbled or mixed up, meaning lacking order, so muddled is a fair synonym.

clue.text: Very large limo, say, as prize

parts.note: OS stands for outsize, a clothing label meaning very large
a limousine is one example of a motor car

explanation.surface: An enormous stretch limousine is awarded as the prize.
explanation.walkthrough: The award is the Academy Award statuette given in Hollywood.
explanation.definitionFit: The film industry's famous statuette is an award, so it is an example of a trophy.

clue.text: Choir screen composed of rose red characters

indicators.note: composed of means made up from, so the letters of rose red are put together in a new order

explanation.surface: A church choir screen made of rose-red lettering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters' says the anagram is of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An ornamental screen behind a church altar, often at the choir end; the clue uses it loosely.

clue.text: Unfinished book marks British Queen's 30-day period

indicators.note: unfinished means the final letter is cut off the word for a book

parts.note: a novel is a book
M is the abbreviation for marks, the old German currency
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen's cipher

explanation.surface: An incomplete book earns marks from the British Queen over a month.
explanation.definitionFit: The eleventh month of the year has thirty days, so it is one such span of the calendar.

clue.text: Signifying average in golf (as 1A)

parts.note: the mean is an average
Golf is the radio alphabet word for G

explanation.surface: Explaining what an average golf score means.
explanation.walkthrough: '(as 1A)' says golf is a radio codeword here, standing for G.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means expressive or significant, as in a knowing look.

clue.text: Reported sudden increases in fabrics

indicators.note: reported means spoken of, so the word is one that sounds like the next one

parts.note: surges are sudden rises

explanation.surface: News of a rise in textile output.
explanation.definitionFit: Serge is a hard-wearing twilled woollen cloth, so the plural names kinds of material.

clue.text: Take sinuous steps to deceive communist

parts.note: to fox someone is to deceive or baffle them
Trot is short for a Trotskyist, a type of communist

explanation.surface: A sly dancer tries to fool a communist with sinuous moves.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to perform the ballroom dance of that name, which uses gliding, weaving steps.

clue.text: Waxy lemon covers woody tissue

indicators.note: covers means encloses, so the letters lie inside the words before it

explanation.surface: A waxed lemon peel encloses the fruit's tissue.
explanation.definitionFit: The botanical term for the water-carrying tissue that forms the wood of plants.

clue.text: According to GIs, Vietcong burn position

parts.note: to char is to burn or scorch
the lie of something is its position, as in the lie of the land

explanation.surface: American soldiers report the Vietcong burning a position.
explanation.definitionFit: US troops in Vietnam used the radio alphabet word for VC as slang for the enemy guerrillas.

clue.text: Song about origins of romantic overwhelming love

parts.note: ca is circa, Latin for about

indicators.note: origins means beginnings, so the opening letters of the next three words are taken

explanation.surface: A ballad about the beginnings of an all-consuming romance.
explanation.definitionFit: A joyful hymn, especially at Christmas, is a kind of festive musical piece.

clue.text: Feds intermingle in a relaxed manner having personal control of outcome

indicators.note: loosely arranged, so the letters of the two words are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: Federal agents casually mixing with others while deciding their own destiny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'intermingle' looks like the anagram signal but is part of the fodder; the signal is 'in a relaxed manner'.
explanation.definitionFit: Deciding one's own fate or course without outside authority; a synonym for autonomous.

clue.text: Sadly I seem resigned in the end to failure

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so just the closing letter of resigned is used
sadly suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters of I seem are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone sadly says they seem resigned to failure in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sadly' turns I SEEM into EMISE, which follows the D from the end of 'resigned'.
explanation.definitionFit: Demise means the end or collapse of something, as in the downfall of a company, so failure fits.

clue.text: Scroungers are essentially rabid tail-enders

indicators.note: essentially means at its core, so only the central letter of rabid is taken

parts.note: laggers are those who trail behind, at the tail end

explanation.surface: Freeloaders described as rabid stragglers at the back.
explanation.definitionFit: Blag is British slang for getting something free by persuasion, so those who do it are cadgers.
